requirement: Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is implemented completely and tested, so I chose true.**

**Implementation**
- `valid_name` (src/lib.rs:778) enforces the name rule. A name must be nonempty and split on `.` into nonempty segments, and each segment may contain only ASCII alphanumerics, `_` or `-`. The check is byte-wise, so non-ASCII text is rejected.
- `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs:520) leaves a `{req}`, `{example}` or `{definition}` directive out of the block list when its local name is invalid. It also requires whitespace between the directive and the name.
- `chapter_namespace` (src/lib.rs:263) strips the extension and joins the path components with `.`. Only when the path has more than one component does it drop a leading `reqs` and a final `index` or `README`. That matches the nested-path rule.
- `full_requirement_name` joins the namespace and the local name.
- `reference_roles` (src/lib.rs:682) emits a `{impl}`, `{cite}`, `{test}` or `{term}` role only when `valid_name` accepts its name. An invalid role stays literal and references nothing. This function backs the book renderer (`replace_references`), CI reference collection and authoring, so the rule applies everywhere roles are read.
- Definitions that build on an invalid full name are also excluded:
  - `preprocess_book` skips a directive whose full name is invalid, so it defines nothing and generates no detail page.
  - `replace_definitions` only rewrites blocks whose full name is valid, so an invalid-namespace directive stays literal in the rendered book.
  - `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs:356) rejects an invalid full name with `continue` after reporting it. It does not define the name or expect evidence for it.
- All of these functions carry `{impl}` markers for `requirements.ci.identifiers`.
- I found no unmarked code that implements part of the requirement. The other users of these helpers (`replace_references`, `missing_function_references`, `terms.rs`, `index.rs`) call the marked `reference_roles` and `definition_blocks`.
- One behavior is not spelled out in this requirement. `collect_definitions` reports an "invalid … name" validation error when a valid local name sits in a chapter with an invalid namespace. This is consistent with the requirement, since the directive is still not defined. It also falls under the CI convention of reporting failed checks, so I did not count it as a gap.

**Tests** (all marked `{test}` for this requirement)
- `chapter_path_prefixes_the_requirement_name` (src/lib.rs:943) covers the namespace cases:
  - `reqs/foo/bar`, `reqs/foo/README`, `reqs/foo/index`, `foo/index` and `reqs/index` (empty namespace) are stripped as specified.
  - `index.md` and `reqs.md` at the top level are kept, because only nested paths are stripped.
  - `other/reqs/a` is kept, because only a leading `reqs/` is stripped.
- `invalid_names_remain_literal` (src/lib.rs:1007) covers literal handling:
  - A bad local name stays literal.
  - A valid local name in an invalid namespace (`a&b`) also stays literal.
  - `valid_name` is tested on invalid names (empty, `a..b`, `.a`, `a.`, space, non-ASCII, `/`, `&`, backtick) and valid names (`a_b.c-d`, `x.-_.y`).
  - All four roles are tested with invalid names and with a valid name.
  - Directive openers with invalid names produce no blocks.
- `chapters_with_invalid_namespaces_define_nothing_in_the_book` (src/lib.rs:1052) runs `preprocess_book` on a chapter at `bad dir/rules.md`. It asserts that no detail page is generated, that the content is unchanged and that the matching role stays literal.
- `invalid_full_names_from_chapter_paths_are_reported_and_not_defined` (src/evidence.rs:2060) checks that a `bad dir` chapter is reported and expects no evidence, and that `reqs/index.md` yields the bare name `top`.
- The remaining marked tests also exercise the rule: `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` (src/evidence.rs:1510) uses a valid nested full name, and `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` (src/lib.rs:1305) checks that a bad example name stays literal.

Together these cover the boundaries and the failure cases. No FIXMEs or acknowledged gaps appear in the supplied sources.
